title: What Comes After Mobile? Meta’s Andrew Bosworth on AI and Consumer Tech

reader_summary.headline: Is there a better way I think there is?
reader_summary.overview: Is there a better way I think there is? Every single interface that I interact with. If you were starting from scratch today, you probably wouldn't build this app-centric world. You can imagine a post phone world. The past 20 years of consumer technology have been a story of apps, of touch screens, and of smartphones.

key_points.text: Every single interface that I interact with.
key_points.evidence_quote: Every single interface that I interact with, every single problem space that I'm trying to solve are going to be made easier by virtue of this new technology.

thesis: Andrew Bosworth argues that the mobile phone form factor is saturated and will likely be replaced by a new AI-enabled stack that is more agentic, adaptive, and immersive. He suggests that while high-end mixed reality experiences will initially be expensive and unevenly distributed, the next wave of consumer technology will run on user intent rather than taps and swipes.
